## Citation

Murphy, J.A., Barrantes-Reynolds, R., Kocherlakota, R., Bond, J.P., & Greenblatt, M.S. (2004). The CDKN2A Database: Integrating Allelic Variants with Evolution, Structure, Function, and Disease Association. *Human Mutation*, 24(4), 296-304.

## Abstract

CDKN2A (p16) mutations are associated with familial melanoma and other cancers. This work presents a comprehensive database integrating genetic variants with evolutionary, structural, functional, and clinical information to facilitate variant interpretation.

## Key Findings

- Database consolidates CDKN2A mutations from literature and public sources
- Integrates evolutionary conservation and protein structural information
- Correlates variants with functional effects and disease phenotypes
- Provides tools for predicting pathogenicity of novel variants

## Role

As a co-author, I contributed to data curation, bioinformatics analysis, and database development.
